pod_concurrency_experiment.narrative: Preflight is separate because it omitted --config=ci. The controlled four-unit arms were 2@4 (13/13 pass) and 3@4 (10 pass, 3 readiness failures from scheduler Insufficient memory at overlap 3; this was request admission capacity, not measured physical OOM). The approved five-action 8-unit sequence (2,3,4,4,2) passed all 13 JUnit cases each time, with OTel-observed peak case overlap 2,3,4,4,2 and storage-first exclusivity in every successful arm. Actual eight-unit RBE requests were 8,000mCPU, 20,000,000,000B RAM and 53,687,091,200B free disk. Setup, TestRunner action wall, OTel case envelope/span sum, teardown, residual, and JUnit item-duration sums are separate clocks. Preflight versus measured config IDs are separately labeled as configured-target and TestResult provenance.

experiment_narrative.headline: k3s reuse is merged; the larger Pod worker remains a candidate.
experiment_narrative.lead_html: Expanded hosted k3s baseline reuse merged in #13586 on 2026-11-02T03:17:13Z. Selected all-suite cold/warm measurements and the executor boundary supersede the Pod-only adoption plan. Fleet effects remain pending soak.
experiment_narrative.pod_conclusion_html: Four slots shortened the case envelope to 100.9–102.6s, versus 128.6/142.8s for the two-slot controls on the same eight-unit worker. The final two-slot control took 227.1s despite a lower 50.4s setup span, compared with the four-slot pair’s 192.0/192.6s actions and 61.8/63.0s setup. That is a selected 34.8s (15.3%) whole-action difference against the final control, not a fleet treatment estimate. The initial two-slot control’s 305.2s action included 149.4s setup, so presenting the full 113s difference as a concurrency saving would be misleading. Four-slot allocation is about 1,538 unit-seconds per action, versus 1,049 for the original four-unit/two-slot control: roughly 47% more allocation for the observed lower wall time. Retain two slots on the existing worker; the eight-unit/four-slot candidate is useful if Pods become the blocking gate after VM improvement. Right-sizing fixture memory requests remains untested and needs per-container peak evidence.
experiment_narrative.recommendation_a_html: A · Measure merged k3s reuse after soak Implementation merged in #13586, including VM and MCP coverage. Selected non-VM action time fell 32–40%; normal VM fell 19%. The warm VM action still took 304s, so this alone does not reach the 186s/265s baseline half-time goals. Adoption is complete; fleet effect and warm hit rate remain pending. Follow the 48-hour checkpoint and measurement plan. Keep fresh fixtures, cold rebuild and ownership checks. Re-rank accelerated guests and Pod slots after observing the new critical path.
experiment_narrative.recommendation_c_html: C · Pod slots after VM improvementThe 2/3/4 experiment is complete. Three slots exceeded scheduler memory reservations on four units. On eight units, four slots passed twice with 101–103s case envelopes and 192–193s actions; the final two-slot control was 143s/227s. Candidate change: CASE_LIMIT=4 plus EstimatedComputeUnits=8; preserve storage exclusivity, all 13 cases and pool ownership.Small source change, doubled requested compute/memory. About 47% more unit-seconds than the original four-unit control in these selected actions. Two passing candidate runs establish neither a fleet flake rate nor gate savings. VM actions remain 344–425s, so this does not deliver 2× CI. Keep the current two-slot worker configuration until the bottleneck shifts or request sizing is measured.
